 # Releasing AlphaCode
 
-Releases are GitHub Releases built from tags. No package version file is edited and no bot commits back to `dev`.
+Releases are GitHub Releases built from tags. The release version is committed to the
+repository before the release is cut: no release step rewrites history and nothing
+commits back to `dev` on your behalf.
+
+## The version source
+
+Root `package.json` holds the one authoritative version. Everything else derives from it
+and is checked against it:
+
+| Surface | Example | Enforced by |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `package.json` (root) | `0.1.0` | `./script/bump.ts` is the only writer |
+| `packages/opencode/package.json` (executable) | `0.1.0` | `./script/bump.ts`, `./script/release-check.ts` |
+| Build / runtime (`alphacode --version`) | `0.1.0` | release guard in `@opencode-ai/script`, `--version` smoke test in `script/build.ts` |
+| Git tag | `v0.1.0` | `./script/release-check.ts --tag v0.1.0` (runs in the publish workflow) |
+
+A release build is always built from the exact tag, so a clean checkout of `vX.Y.Z`
+reports `X.Y.Z` both from package metadata and from `alphacode --version`.
+
+`0.1.0` is the inherited baseline. Local-only builds that were never committed, tagged
+or released stay that way - no historical releases are manufactured for them.
 
 ## Cut a release
 
-Use **Actions → publish → Run workflow** and select `dev`. Normally run `script/release` (auto bump), or choose an explicit `patch`, `minor`, or `major` bump. To preview first, run `script/release minor --dry-run`; dry runs are allowed from any ref and create no release. You can also set `VERSION=1.2.3` to override the version.
+From a clean `dev` checkout, in this exact order:
+
+```bash
+# 1. Bump the authoritative version (deterministic SemVer; rewrites both package.json files)
+./script/bump.ts patch                 # or minor / major / auto / X.Y.Z
+
+# 2. Commit and push - the release tag is created at this commit
+git add package.json packages/opencode/package.json
+git commit -m "chore(release): v<version>"
+git push origin dev
+
+# 3. Preview the release notes (allowed from any ref; creates nothing)
+./script/release --dry-run
+
+# 4. Cut the release (dev only): creates the draft release and the tag, builds every
+#    target from that tag, attaches the archives, then publishes
+./script/release
+```
+
+Step 4 is a `gh workflow run publish.yml --ref dev` dispatch; the workflow itself runs
+`./script/version.ts` (notes + draft release + tag) and then
+`./packages/opencode/script/build.ts` from a checkout of the tag.
 
-Auto bump examines conventional commits on the first-parent history since the last `vX.Y.Z` tag:
+### Choosing the bump
+
+- `patch` / `minor` / `major`: explicit SemVer bump of the committed version.
+- `auto`: derives the bump from conventional commits on the first-parent history since
+  the last `vX.Y.Z` tag.
+- `X.Y.Z`: explicit target version.
+
+`auto` needs a previous tag, so the first AlphaCode release must be an explicit
+`patch`, `minor`, `major`, or `X.Y.Z`. `./script/bump.ts` refuses to move the version
+backwards, to bump to a prerelease, or to reuse a version that already has a tag.
 
 | Commit | Bump |
 | --- | --- |
@@ -15,18 +65,58 @@ Auto bump examines conventional commits on the first-parent history since the la
 | `type!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer | minor while the current major is 0; major once it is at least 1 |
 | Other types | no bump |
 
-`auto` fails when there are no releasable commits. Auto bump never moves version 0 to 1; use an explicit `version=1.0.0` when making that transition.
+`auto` fails when there are no releasable commits. It never moves version 0 to 1; use an
+explicit version for that transition.
+
+## Version checks
+
+```bash
+./script/release-check.ts                 # package metadata, plus the tag at HEAD if any
+./script/release-check.ts --tag v0.1.1    # package metadata against an exact tag
+```
+
+The check exits non-zero and lists every disagreement (root vs executable package,
+package vs tag, package vs runtime). It runs in both publish jobs, so a release whose
+tag, package metadata and embedded version disagree cannot be built.
+
+A development build can never publish a release: the build only uploads artifacts when
+`ALPHACODE_RELEASE` is set, and `@opencode-ai/script` refuses to start a release build
+whose version is not the exact, stable, committed package version.
+
+## Environment variables
+
+| Variable | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ALPHACODE_VERSION` | Version to build/embed; in a release build it must equal `package.json` |
+| `ALPHACODE_BUMP` | `auto`, `patch`, `minor` or `major`; forces the release channel |
+| `ALPHACODE_CHANNEL` | `latest` for release builds; anything else is a development build |
+| `ALPHACODE_RELEASE` | Truthy to attach build artifacts to the release |
+
+The inherited `OPENCODE_VERSION`, `OPENCODE_BUMP`, `OPENCODE_CHANNEL` and
+`OPENCODE_RELEASE_ID` names are still accepted as compatibility aliases (the nix
+derivation uses them), but setting an alias and its `ALPHACODE_*` name to different
+values is an error, not a silent choice.
 
-## First tracked release
+## Reproduce a release
 
-The first release establishes the tag baseline. On `dev`, run the workflow once with `version=0.2.0` and `dry_run=true`; verify the summary, then repeat with `dry_run=false`. Do not create a tag or edit a `package.json` by hand.
+```bash
+git checkout v<version>
+./script/release-check.ts --tag v<version>
+cd packages/opencode && bun run script/build.ts --single
+./dist/alphacode-linux-x64/bin/alphacode --version   # prints <version>
+```

+before the first tag). Preview/local builds do not check for or install updates.
 
-Release builds check this repository's latest GitHub Release. Patch updates install automatically by default; major and minor updates notify instead. Set `autoupdate: "notify"` in the user config to notify for patch updates too.
+Release builds check this repository's latest GitHub Release. Patch updates install
+automatically by default; major and minor updates notify instead. Set
+`autoupdate: "notify"` in the user config to notify for patch updates too.
 
 ## Failures and hotfixes
 
-A failed build leaves no published release: the `cleanup` job deletes a leftover draft. A hotfix is an ordinary release from `dev`: merge or cherry-pick the fix into `dev`, then cut a normal patch release.
+A failed build leaves no published release: the `cleanup` job deletes a leftover draft.
+A hotfix is an ordinary release from `dev`: merge or cherry-pick the fix into `dev`,
+then cut a normal patch release.

+import { parseVersion, type BumpInput } from "./version"
+
+/**
+ * AlphaCode release environment variables.
+ *
+ * `ALPHACODE_*` is the documented interface. The `OPENCODE_*` names survive as
+ * compatibility aliases for inherited OpenCode tooling (nix derivations, older
+ * workflow snippets), but they must never disagree with the AlphaCode name.
+ */
+export const ENV_NAMES = {
+  version: ["ALPHACODE_VERSION", "OPENCODE_VERSION"],
+  bump: ["ALPHACODE_BUMP", "OPENCODE_BUMP"],
+  channel: ["ALPHACODE_CHANNEL", "OPENCODE_CHANNEL"],
+  release: ["ALPHACODE_RELEASE", "ALPHACODE_RELEASE_ID", "OPENCODE_RELEASE", "OPENCODE_RELEASE_ID"],
+} as const
+
+export type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>
+
+export class EnvConflictError extends Error {
+  constructor(message: string) {
+    super(message)
+    this.name = "EnvConflictError"
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Reads the first populated name, rejecting disagreeing aliases.
+ */
+export function envValue(env: Env, names: readonly string[]): string | undefined {
+  const found = names
+    .map((name) => ({ name, value: env[name]?.trim() }))
+    .filter((entry): entry is { name: string; value: string } => entry.value !== undefined && entry.value !== "")
+
+  if (found.length === 0) return undefined
+
+  const distinct = [...new Set(found.map((entry) => entry.value))]
+  if (distinct.length > 1) {
+    throw new EnvConflictError(
+      `Conflicting environment values: ${found.map((entry) => `${entry.name}=${entry.value}`).join(", ")}. Set exactly one of ${names.join(", ")}.`,
+    )
+  }
+
+  return distinct[0]
+}
+
+export function resolveBump(raw: string | undefined): BumpInput | undefined {
+  const input = raw?.trim().toLowerCase()
+  if (!input) return undefined
+  if (input === "auto" || input === "patch" || input === "minor" || input === "major") return input
+  throw new Error(`Invalid bump: ${raw}. Expected auto, patch, minor, or major.`)
+}
+
+export function resolveVersion(raw: string | undefined): string | undefined {
+  const input = raw?.trim()
+  if (!input) return undefined
+  // Throws when the override is not SemVer.
+  parseVersion(input)
+  return input.replace(/^v/, "")
+}
+
+export function resolveRelease(env: Env): boolean {
+  return ENV_NAMES.release.some((name) => {
+    const value = env[name]?.trim()
+    return value !== undefined && value !== "" && value !== "0" && value !== "false"
+  })
+}
+
+export interface ReleaseEnv {
+  version?: string
+  bump?: BumpInput
+  channel?: string
+  release: boolean
+}
+
+/**
+ * Resolves every release input from the environment. Pure: safe to unit test
+ * and free of git or filesystem access.
+ */
+export function resolveEnv(env: Env = process.env as Env): ReleaseEnv {
+  const version = resolveVersion(envValue(env, ENV_NAMES.version))
+  const bump = resolveBump(envValue(env, ENV_NAMES.bump))
+  const channel = envValue(env, ENV_NAMES.channel)
+
+  return {
+    ...(version === undefined ? {} : { version }),
+    ...(bump === undefined ? {} : { bump }),
+    ...(channel === undefined ? {} : { channel }),
+    release: resolveRelease(env),
+  }
+}

+/**
+ * The release tag pointing at `sha`, if any. Used to recognise a release build
+ * from an exact tag checkout, where `git branch --show-current` is empty.
+ */
+export async function tagAtHead(sha: string = "HEAD", cwd = process.cwd()): Promise<string | null> {
+  const tags = await $`git tag --points-at ${sha} --list 'v[0-9]*' --sort=-v:refname`
+    .cwd(cwd)
+    .nothrow()
+    .text()
+  return (
+    tags
+      .split(/\r?\n/)
+      .map((tag) => tag.trim())
+      .find((tag) => TAG_RE.test(tag)) ?? null
+  )
+}
+

   const output = tag
     ? await $`git log --first-parent --format=%H%x1f%s%x1f%b%x1e ${tag}..${sha}`.cwd(cwd).text()

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..82476ca43f5d23a3542480a26d75a09fa2f47051
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/script/src/release.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+import { parseVersion, TAG_RE } from "./version"
+
+/**
+ * A release version is an exact SemVer release: no prerelease, no build
+ * metadata. Development builds (`X.Y.Z-dev.N+<sha>`) are never release versions.
+ */
+export function isReleaseVersion(version: string): boolean {
+  return parseVersion(version).pre === undefined
+}
+
+export function tagForVersion(version: string): string {
+  return `v${version}`
+}
+
+export class ReleaseValidationError extends Error {
+  readonly problems: string[]
+
+  constructor(problems: string[]) {
+    super(`Release version validation failed:\n${problems.map((problem) => `  - ${problem}`).join("\n")}`)
+    this.name = "ReleaseValidationError"
+    this.problems = problems
+  }
+}
+
+export interface ReleaseFacts {
+  /** Root `package.json` version: the single authoritative metadata source. */
+  packageVersion: string
+  /** `packages/opencode/package.json` version: the executable package metadata. */
+  executableVersion?: string
+  /** Version reported at runtime (`alphacode --version` / `Script.version`). */
+  runtimeVersion?: string
+  /** Git tag the release is built from, e.g. `v0.1.1`. */
+  tag?: string
+}
+
+/**
+ * Collects every package/runtime/tag disagreement. Returns an empty array when
+ * all supplied facts describe one and the same release version.
+ */
+export function validateReleaseVersions(facts: ReleaseFacts): string[] {
+  const problems: string[] = []
+  const packageVersion = facts.packageVersion
+
+  try {
+    parseVersion(packageVersion)
+  } catch {
+    problems.push(`root package.json version ${JSON.stringify(packageVersion)} is not valid SemVer`)
+    return problems
+  }
+
+  if (!isReleaseVersion(packageVersion)) {
+    problems.push(
+      `root package.json version ${packageVersion} is a prerelease; a release builds from a stable version (run ./script/bump.ts)`,
+    )
+  }
+
+  if (facts.executableVersion !== undefined && facts.executableVersion !== packageVersion) {
+    problems.push(
+      `packages/opencode/package.json version ${facts.executableVersion} does not match root package.json version ${packageVersion}`,
+    )
+  }
+
+  if (facts.tag !== undefined) {
+    if (!TAG_RE.test(facts.tag)) {
+      problems.push(`tag ${facts.tag} is not a release tag (expected vX.Y.Z)`)
+    } else if (facts.tag !== tagForVersion(packageVersion)) {
+      problems.push(
+        `tag ${facts.tag} does not match root package.json version ${packageVersion} (expected ${tagForVersion(packageVersion)})`,
+      )
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (facts.runtimeVersion !== undefined && facts.runtimeVersion !== packageVersion) {
+    problems.push(`runtime version ${facts.runtimeVersion} does not match root package.json version ${packageVersion}`)
+  }
+
+  return problems
+}
+
+export function assertReleaseVersions(facts: ReleaseFacts): void {
+  const problems = validateReleaseVersions(facts)
+  if (problems.length > 0) throw new ReleaseValidationError(problems)
+}

+import path from "node:path"

+const cleanEnv = (extra: Record<string, string> = {}) => {
+  const env: Record<string, string> = { ...process.env } as Record<string, string>
+  for (const names of Object.values(ENV_NAMES)) {
+    for (const name of names) delete env[name]
+  }
+  delete env.GITHUB_REF
+  delete env.GITHUB_REF_NAME
+  return { ...env, ...extra }

+    expect(resolveEnv({ OPENCODE_VERSION: "v0.1.1" }).version).toBe("0.1.1")
+    expect(resolveEnv({ ALPHACODE_VERSION: "0.1.1", OPENCODE_VERSION: "0.1.1" }).version).toBe("0.1.1")

+  })

+  test("rejects disagreeing aliases instead of picking one silently", () => {
+    expect(() => resolveEnv({ ALPHACODE_VERSION: "0.1.1", OPENCODE_VERSION: "0.2.0" })).toThrow(EnvConflictError)
+    expect(() => resolveEnv({ ALPHACODE_CHANNEL: "latest", OPENCODE_CHANNEL: "dev" })).toThrow(EnvConflictError)
+    expect(() => envValue({ A: "1", B: "2" }, ["A", "B"])).toThrow(EnvConflictError)
+  })

+    expect(() => resolveVersion("1.2")).toThrow()
+    expect(() => resolveVersion("01.2.3")).toThrow()
+  })

+    const expected = input.trim().toLowerCase() as BumpInput
+    expect(resolveBump(input)).toBe(expected)
+  })

+  test("rejects unknown bumps and leaves an unset bump unset", () => {
+    expect(resolveBump(undefined)).toBeUndefined()
+    expect(resolveBump("   ")).toBeUndefined()
+    expect(() => resolveBump("huge")).toThrow(/Invalid bump/)
+  })

+    expect(resolveEnv({ ALPHACODE_RELEASE: "1" }).release).toBe(true)
+    expect(resolveEnv({ OPENCODE_RELEASE_ID: "12345" }).release).toBe(true)
+    expect(resolveEnv({ ALPHACODE_RELEASE: "false" }).release).toBe(false)

+        executableVersion: "0.1.1",

+      "tag v0.1.2 does not match root package.json version 0.1.1 (expected v0.1.1)",
+      "runtime version 0.1.3 does not match root package.json version 0.1.1",
+    ])
+  })

+    expect(validateReleaseVersions({ packageVersion: "0.1.1", tag: "vscode-v9.9.9" })).toEqual([

+      expect(failure.problems).toHaveLength(1)
+      expect(failure.message).toContain("does not match root package.json version 0.1.1")
+    }
+  })
+})

+describe("release vs development versions", () => {
+  test("a development version is never a release version", () => {
+    const dev = devVersion("v0.1.0", 3, "abc1234", false)
+    expect(dev).toBe("0.1.1-dev.3+abc1234")
+    expect(isReleaseVersion(dev)).toBe(false)
+    expect(isReleaseVersion(devVersion("v0.1.0", 3, "abc1234", true))).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  test("a bumped version is a release version", () => {
+    expect(isReleaseVersion(bumpVersion("0.1.0", "patch"))).toBe(true)
+    expect(isReleaseVersion("0.1.0")).toBe(true)
+    expect(isReleaseVersion("1.2.3-rc.1")).toBe(false)
+    expect(tagForVersion("0.1.1")).toBe("v0.1.1")
+  })
+
+  test("a development version cannot be published as a release", () => {
+    expect(() =>
+      assertReleaseVersions({ packageVersion: "0.1.1", runtimeVersion: devVersion("v0.1.1", 1, "abc1234", false) }),
+    ).toThrow(ReleaseValidationError)
+  })
+})
+
+const probe = async (extra: Record<string, string> = {}) => {
+  const proc = Bun.spawn(
+    [
+      "bun",
+      "-e",
+      'const { Script } = await import("@opencode-ai/script"); console.log("PROBE " + JSON.stringify({ channel: Script.channel, version: Script.version, packageVersion: Script.packageVersion, preview: Script.preview, release: Script.release }))',
+    ],
+    { cwd: repoRoot, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe", env: cleanEnv(extra) },
+  )
+  const [stdout, stderr, exitCode] = await Promise.all([
+    new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
+    new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
+    proc.exited,
+  ])
+  const line = stdout.split(/\r?\n/).find((item) => item.startsWith("PROBE "))
+  return {
+    exitCode,
+    stderr,
+    ...(line
+      ? { result: JSON.parse(line.slice("PROBE ".length)) as Record<string, string | boolean> }
+      : { result: undefined }),
+  }
+}
+
+const runCheck = async (args: string[]) => {
+  const proc = Bun.spawn(["bun", "run", path.join(repoRoot, "script", "release-check.ts"), ...args], {
+    cwd: repoRoot,
+    stdout: "pipe",
+    stderr: "pipe",
+    env: cleanEnv(),
+  })
+  const [stdout, stderr, exitCode] = await Promise.all([
+    new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
+    new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
+    proc.exited,
+  ])
+  return { exitCode, stdout, stderr }
+}
+
+describe("release scripts", () => {
+  test(
+    "a release build reports the committed package version",
+    async () => {
+      const { exitCode, result, stderr } = await probe({ ALPHACODE_VERSION: packageVersion })
+      expect(exitCode).toBe(0)
+      expect(result).toEqual({
+        channel: "latest",
+        version: packageVersion,
+        packageVersion,
+        preview: false,
+        release: false,
+      })
+      expect(stderr).not.toContain("Release version validation failed")
+
+      const alias = await probe({ OPENCODE_VERSION: packageVersion })
+      expect(alias.exitCode).toBe(0)
+      expect(alias.result).toEqual(result)
+    },
+    120_000,
+  )
+
+  test(
+    "a development build never reports a stable release version",
+    async () => {
+      const { exitCode, result } = await probe({ ALPHACODE_CHANNEL: "dev" })
+      expect(exitCode).toBe(0)
+      expect(result?.preview).toBe(true)
+      expect(result?.release).toBe(false)
+      expect(result?.packageVersion).toBe(packageVersion)
+      expect(String(result?.version)).toMatch(/-dev\./)
+    },
+    120_000,
+  )
+
+  test(
+    "publishing is refused when the runtime version disagrees with package metadata",
+    async () => {
+      const { exitCode, stderr } = await probe({ ALPHACODE_RELEASE: "1", ALPHACODE_VERSION: otherVersion })
+      expect(exitCode).not.toBe(0)
+      expect(stderr).toContain("Release version validation failed")
+      expect(stderr).toContain("does not match root package.json version")
+    },
+    120_000,
+  )
+
+  test(
+    "release-check accepts the repository version and rejects a mismatched tag",
+    async () => {
+      const ok = await runCheck(["--tag", tagForVersion(packageVersion)])
+      expect(ok.exitCode).toBe(0)
+      expect(ok.stdout).toContain(`release-check ok: ${packageVersion}`)
+
+      const mismatch = await runCheck(["--tag", tagForVersion(otherVersion)])
+      expect(mismatch.exitCode).toBe(1)
+      expect(mismatch.stderr).toContain("does not match root package.json version")
+    },
+    120_000,
+  )
+
+})

+#!/usr/bin/env bun
+
+/**
+ * Deterministic SemVer bump of the single authoritative version source.
+ *
+ *   ./script/bump.ts patch            # 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1
+ *   ./script/bump.ts minor            # 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0
+ *   ./script/bump.ts major            # 0.1.0 -> 1.0.0
+ *   ./script/bump.ts auto             # derive the bump from conventional commits since the last vX.Y.Z tag
+ *   ./script/bump.ts 0.2.0            # explicit version
+ *   ./script/bump.ts patch --dry-run  # print only, write nothing
+ *
+ * Root `package.json` and the executable package (`packages/opencode/package.json`)
+ * are written together so package metadata can never disagree with itself.
+ */
+
+import { $ } from "bun"
+import path from "path"
+import { commitsSince, lastTag } from "../packages/script/src/git"
+import { bumpVersion, nextVersion, parseVersion, type Bump } from "../packages/script/src/version"
+import { isReleaseVersion, tagForVersion } from "../packages/script/src/release"
+
+const root = path.resolve(import.meta.dir, "..")
+const rootPkgPath = path.join(root, "package.json")
+const executablePkgPath = path.join(root, "packages", "opencode", "package.json")
+
+const args = process.argv.slice(2)
+const dryRun = args.includes("--dry-run")
+const input = args.find((arg) => !arg.startsWith("--")) ?? "patch"
+
+const BUMP_TYPES: string[] = ["auto", "patch", "minor", "major"]
+const readVersion = async (file: string): Promise<string> => (await Bun.file(file).json()).version
+
+const compare = (left: string, right: string): number => {
+  const a = parseVersion(left)
+  const b = parseVersion(right)
+  for (const key of ["major", "minor", "patch"] as const) {
+    if (a[key] !== b[key]) return a[key] - b[key]
+  }
+  return 0
+}
+
+const current = await readVersion(rootPkgPath)
+try {
+  parseVersion(current)
+} catch {
+  throw new Error(`Root package.json version ${current} is not valid SemVer`)
+}
+
+const next = await (async (): Promise<string> => {
+  if (!BUMP_TYPES.includes(input)) {
+    const candidate = input.replace(/^v/, "")
+    parseVersion(candidate)
+    if (!isReleaseVersion(candidate)) throw new Error(`Refusing to bump to a prerelease version: ${candidate}`)
+    return candidate
+  }
+
+  if (input === "auto") {
+    const last = await lastTag("HEAD")
+    if (!last) {
+      throw new Error(
+        "No v* tag found; pass an explicit bump (patch, minor, major) or version instead of auto for the first release.",
+      )
+    }
+    return nextVersion(last, await commitsSince(last, "HEAD"), "auto")
+  }
+
+  return bumpVersion(current, input as Bump)
+})()
+
+if (!isReleaseVersion(next)) throw new Error(`Refusing to bump to a prerelease version: ${next}`)
+if (compare(next, current) <= 0) {
+  throw new Error(`Refusing to move the version backwards: ${current} -> ${next}. Pass a higher version.`)
+}
+
+const tag = tagForVersion(next)
+const existing = await $`git rev-parse -q --verify refs/tags/${tag}`.nothrow().text()
+if (existing.trim()) {
+  throw new Error(`Tag ${tag} already exists at ${existing.trim()}. Choose a higher version.`)
+}
+
+const writeVersion = async (file: string) => {
+  const text = await Bun.file(file).text()
+  const pattern = /^([ \t]*"version"[ \t]*:[ \t]*")([^"]*)(")/m
+  const match = pattern.exec(text)
+  if (!match) throw new Error(`No version field found in ${file}`)
+  if (match[2] !== current) throw new Error(`${file} declares ${match[2]}, expected ${current}`)
+  const updated = text.replace(pattern, (_, prefix: string, _value: string, suffix: string) => `${prefix}${next}${suffix}`)
+  if (!dryRun) await Bun.file(file).write(updated)
+}
+
+await writeVersion(rootPkgPath)
+await writeVersion(executablePkgPath)
+
+if (!dryRun) {
+  for (const file of [rootPkgPath, executablePkgPath]) {
+    const written = await readVersion(file)
+    if (written !== next) throw new Error(`${file} reports ${written} after the bump, expected ${next}`)
+  }
+}
+
+const label = dryRun ? "dry-run" : "bump"
+console.log(`${label}: ${current} -> ${next} (${input})`)
+if (dryRun) process.exit(0)
+
+console.log(`updated ${path.relative(root, rootPkgPath)}`)
+console.log(`updated ${path.relative(root, executablePkgPath)}`)
+console.log(`next: git commit -am "chore(release): ${tag}" && git push origin dev, then run ./script/release`)

--- a/script/release
+++ b/script/release

+#

     *)
-      echo "Unknown release argument '$a'; expected auto, patch, minor, major, or --dry-run." >&2

       exit 2
       ;;
   esac

-if [[ -n "${VERSION:-}" ]]; then
-  args+=(-f "version=$VERSION")
-fi
-"${args[@]}"

new file mode 100755
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..406586248b2e1d97ebbd95a51fe4b06362987455

+#!/usr/bin/env bun
+
+/**
+ * Release version check.
+ *
+ * Validates that package metadata and the release tag describe the same version:
+ *
+ *   ./script/release-check.ts                 # package metadata (+ the tag at HEAD)
+ *   ./script/release-check.ts --tag v0.1.1    # package metadata against an exact tag
+ *
+ * Exits non-zero and lists every disagreement. Reads and writes nothing.
+ * The runtime half of the chain is enforced by the release guard in
+ * `@opencode-ai/script` and by the `--version` smoke test in the build.
+ */
+
+import { $ } from "bun"
+import path from "path"
+import { TAG_RE } from "../packages/script/src/version"
+import { assertReleaseVersions, ReleaseValidationError } from "../packages/script/src/release"
+
+const root = path.resolve(import.meta.dir, "..")
+
+const args = process.argv.slice(2)
+const readFlag = (name: string) => {
+  const index = args.indexOf(name)
+  return index === -1 ? undefined : args[index + 1]
+}
+
+let tag = readFlag("--tag")
+
+const rootPkg = await Bun.file(path.join(root, "package.json")).json()
+const executablePkg = await Bun.file(path.join(root, "packages", "opencode", "package.json")).json()
+
+// CI builds run from an exact tag checkout; locally fall back to the tag at HEAD.
+if (!tag && process.env.GITHUB_REF?.startsWith("refs/tags/")) tag = process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME
+if (!tag) {
+  const tags = await $`git tag --points-at HEAD --list 'v[0-9]*' --sort=-v:refname`.nothrow().text()
+  tag =
+    tags
+      .split(/\r?\n/)
+      .map((item) => item.trim())
+      .find((item) => TAG_RE.test(item)) || undefined
+}
+
+try {
+  assertReleaseVersions({
+    packageVersion: rootPkg.version,
+    executableVersion: executablePkg.version,
+    ...(tag ? { tag } : {}),
+  })
+} catch (error) {
+  if (error instanceof ReleaseValidationError) {
+    console.error(error.message)
+    process.exit(1)
+  }
+  throw error
+}
+
+console.log(`release-check ok: ${rootPkg.version}${tag ? ` (tag ${tag})` : ""}`)
